A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original language-model training, factual-recall and slope-calculation experiments, scaling analyses, and evaluations of subsampling and compact knowledge mixing.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains those original results and adds validation-loss analyses, three-seed replication results and Max-over-N reasoning experiments in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The model architectures, random subsampling and compact knowledge mixing procedures remain unchanged. Appendix E.7 explains how CKM preserves the existing token budget; it does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds Max-over-N, which requires selecting the maximum of 30 integers, alongside the retained slope-calculation task (Appendix D.3). The biography datasets, web corpora, PopQA and downstream task coverage remain.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain their random-guess controls, original Pythia checkpoints, web-only models and comparisons without subsampling or CKM. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: v2 introduces SynBio validation-loss measurements and the Max-over-N protocol, including 3M tokens added to OpenWebMath and 1,000 test examples. Section 3.2 also reverses the reported biography exposures for 70M/410M models from approximately 200/3,000 to 3,000/200; this correction does not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Figure 10 checks whether transitions persist with continuous loss. Appendix D.3 adds training-coverage analysis for slope calculation and a larger-input-space experiment to investigate generalization beyond memorized examples. The original hyperparameter ablations are retained, moving from Section 3.3 to Appendix D.2.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 reports three-seed replication of Figure 2(a), with mean accuracy and standard deviation across eight mixing ratios. v1 lacks this seed-based assessment, although downstream uncertainty and scaling-fit intervals already appear in both versions.

E6.justification: v2 adds SynBio loss curves, seed-aggregate results such as 40.4% mean accuracy with 3.1 percentage-point standard deviation at r=0.4, and approximately 60% Max-over-N accuracy for the 70M model at r=0.5. Existing plotted results and numerical Tables 1–4, renumbered 2–5, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mutual-information capacity formulation, mixture assumptions, Theorems 4.2–4.3 and supporting proofs are retained. Appendix D becomes Appendix F, with formatting and cross-reference changes but no substantive revision to the mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly extends the empirical phase-transition claim to continuous validation loss. Section 7 also specifies applicability at the level of individual facts or reasoning procedures. The abstract's central capacity-allocation, threshold-scaling and data-mixing claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D.3 adds quantitative arguments interpreting reasoning performance as generalization beyond memorized input-output pairs. New Appendix A acknowledges that computational costs prevent repeating all experiments across seeds. Section 7 refines how heterogeneous real-world data may conceal transitions for individual knowledge items.

D1.justification: Appendix E.7 newly explains proportional epoch reduction under fixed-budget CKM and its approximate fact-frequency multipliers. v2 also makes WikiBio first-paragraph retention explicit and supplies Max-over-N construction details and an example in Table 13. Existing hardware and general training settings remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Hao, Mizrahi, Su, Kimi Team and Zucchet, supporting discussion of data reformulation, task alignment and knowledge-learning dynamics. Section 6.3 explicitly relates CKM to Su et al.'s data synthesis approach, while the broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 edits setup, strategy and discussion paragraphs, moves ablations and WikiBio evaluation details into appendices, and adds limitations, broader-impact and funding sections. The overall narrative remains recognizable. Some cross-references incorrectly call definitions or lemmas theorems, including Definition F.5.

P2.justification: v2 adds validation-loss Figure 10, Max-over-N Figure 12, seed-statistics Table 1 and task-example Table 13. Existing displays are retained and repositioned, including the ablation figure moved to Appendix D.2. A strategy legend is reworded, with limited layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides additional evidence addressing accuracy-metric artifacts, seed variability and memorization-based explanations through Figure 10, Table 1 and Appendix D.3. Clearer CKM implementation details and explicit replication limitations improve reproducibility and transparency. These limited gains outweigh the newly imprecise theorem cross-references; the central methods, theory and existing results remain stable.
